newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: WTO head urges Mercosur to push for global trade.
newsitem.headline: WTO head urges Mercosur to push for global trade.

text.p: Renato Ruggiero, the Director-General of the World Trade Organization Thursday urged the Mercosur customs union to help build a global trading system.

"Each of you - and all of you - in Mercosur share in the responsibility for constructing this architecture (of global free trade) of the future," Ruggiero said in a speech delivered at a Mercosur presidential summit in Asuncion, the capital of Paraguay.
The Mercosur customs union, established in 1991, groups Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile and Bolivia have free trade agreements with the bloc.

"Once we have agreed to free trade in Mercosur, in the Asia-Pacific region, in North America and in Europe, it is difficult to see our ultimate goal as anything other than a single world market - global free trade," Ruggiero said in a prepared text of his speech.
Ruggiero recognised that globalization and technological change have led to painful adjustment in some countries leading to unemployment and social pressures.
"But these challenges are eclipsed by the immense opportunities that globalization offers," he said.
The head of the global trade body added that Mercosur'ss success will be measures by its participation in the global trade system.

"More and more, Mercosur's success will be measured by your ability to help design and build this new economic order - both in terms of your own interests, and in the interests of the global economy as a whole," he said.
The Mercosur integration process will also "help to amplify and harmonize your voice in the global system," Ruggiero said.
He reiterated comments made to journalists Wednesday, saying "there is every sign that Mercosur will remain one of the most successful and fastest-moving integration processes into the next century."

"Through your leadership, Mercosur has emerged as one of the most dynamic and imaginative initiatives on the world stage today. Surging trade, rising investment, expanding output - every economic indicator points to Mercosur's remarkable achievement in just five years," he told the presidents.
